claims.label: Breach of Quiet Enjoyment / Constructive Eviction
claims.note: Fact-intensive claim, informed by comparable cases rather than a formula -- see cited cases.

claims.label: Breach of Implied Warranty of Suitability
claims.note: Texas recognizes an implied warranty of suitability for commercial leases (Davidow v. Inwood North Professional Group-Phase I, 747 S.W.2d 373 (Tex. 1988)), but it is a default, waivable term -- whether an express lease provision addresses this condition (which would narrow or eliminate the claim) hasn't been confirmed here.

claims.label: Wrongfully Withheld Security Deposit
claims.note: Most states have no commercial-specific deposit statute -- this is usually a straight lease-terms question, not a statutory one.

extractedFacts.wrongfulLockoutCitation: Tex. Prop. Code Sec. 93.002/93.003 -- actual damages + greater of one month's rent or $500, plus reasonable attorney's fees and costs.

outcome.description: After a four-day jury trial the jury found Section 3(c) was a condition precedent that Empower failed to satisfy; the trial court rendered judgment declaring the lease abrogated and ordered Empower to pay Covenant $96,291.09 in damages (the deposit), $611,491.45 in attorney's fees, and $135,000 in conditional appellate fees. The court of appeals held Section 3(c) is a covenant, not a condition precedent, reversed the entire judgment, rendered take-nothing on the condition-precedent declarations, and remanded the remaining declarations, the damages and fee awards, and Empower's breach-of-contract counterclaim.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed and remanded; no final figure yet.
